resources.string: This account has nothing in its libraries yet, or they have not been synced. Refresh to try again.
This device is offline and nothing has been downloaded for this account yet. Your library will appear once the connection returns.
Sign in to an Audiobookshelf server to see your books.
Show all books as a list
No book in your libraries matches that search.
Showing cached content. The last refresh failed.
This profile needs to sign in again. Your library is shown from the last sync.
Enter the address of your Audiobookshelf server.
For example books.example.com. HTTPS is used unless you type http://
This server did not report its version.
No scheme was typed, so HTTPS was used.
This connection is not encrypted. Your password and your listening data would cross the network in the clear.
Each address is checked again when you pick it.
Connect an Audiobookshelf server to add one.
This deletes this profile\'s saved session, listening progress and downloads from this device. Nothing is deleted from the server, and other profiles are not affected.
Show all books again instead of %1$s
Nothing in this library matches your search.
This series is not in the current profile\'s library.
This book is no longer in the cached library.

This sends the book back to the beginning, on this device and on your server. No audio files are deleted, nothing is removed from your library, and any download stays where it is. You can start listening again from anywhere.
Everything here comes from your own server\'s metadata. A blank field is one the server has not filled in.
This book has no chapter information.
Everything that has happened in this book, here and on your other devices. Tap a row to go back to where it started.
Nothing yet. Playing, seeking, changing chapter or setting a sleep timer will appear here.
%1$s from %2$s to %3$s. Tap to return to %2$s.
Places you kept in this book. Tap one to go back to it.
No bookmarks yet. The button above keeps wherever you are in the book.
Playback stopped. The server or the connection may be unavailable.
Books you download appear here, with how much space each one uses. Download one from its own screen.
This applies to the next download. Books already on this device stay where they are and keep playing. Books on a card you take out will offer to download again — nothing is deleted.
Checks that every downloaded file is still present, the right size, and openable as audio. It does not compare the audio with your server — Audiobookshelf does not send a checksum to compare against.
A book in a library this profile cannot see
Keep this one, never delete it automatically
This removes the book from your downloads. Another profile on this phone downloaded it too, so the files stay and no space is freed until they remove it as well. Nothing is deleted on your server.
Both of these are off until you turn them on. One spends space and data on a book you did not ask for; the other deletes a book you did.
Download the next book in a series
When you pass halfway through a book, the next one in the same series starts downloading.
Remove the previous book in the series
When the next book arrives, the one before the book you are listening to is removed from this device. Never the one playing.
A finished book is removed this long after you finished it. Never the book playing, never one whose progress has not reached your server, and never one you have pinned.
Wi-Fi is always used when it is available. These decide what may also use mobile data. Your phone decides what counts as mobile data, so a Wi-Fi network you marked as metered is treated the same way.
Download next book over mobile data
BookWave appears in Android Auto with three tabs: Continue, Chapters and History. It always opens on the book you were last listening to.
Start playing when a car connects
Rewind when the timer stops playback
If you fall asleep, the book winds back by this much so you can pick up something you remember. Off by default.
Off by default. When it is on, the app senses motion only while a timer is running — never at other times.
No sleep timers have been set on this device yet.
Kept on this device only, and never sent anywhere.
Ran down and paused the book
The app closed while it was running

The audio files come off this device and the space is freed. Nothing is deleted on your server, your position is kept, and you can download it again whenever you like. If another profile on this phone downloaded the same book, their copy stays.
A work in progress. Streaming and offline playback, chapters, bookmarks, the sleep timer, downloads and progress sync are built; the management tools are not.

What happens during a navigation prompt or a notification sound. Pausing means you miss nothing; keeping it playing means you have nothing to rewind. A phone call pauses the book either way — that is Android\'s decision, not this app\'s. A change applies the next time a book starts.

Nothing is the default: opening the app to look at your library does not put a player in your notification shade. The play button on your headphones starts your last book whichever of these you choose.
Times playback ran out of buffer
Last wait before a book started
A larger buffer should make the first number smaller and the others larger. No book titles are recorded here.

Each headset, speaker or car gets its own answer. New devices start at Ready — the book is loaded and paused, so the play button on your headphones starts it instantly. A device appears here the first time you connect it.
No devices yet. Connect headphones, a speaker or a car and it will appear here.
Auto-play is best effort. Android and some manufacturers stop apps running in the background, which can prevent a connection from starting a book when the app has not been opened for a while.
This is a speaker, so a book will start out loud in whatever room it is in.
Changing the icon does not interrupt anything that is playing. Your home screen may take a moment to catch up, and an icon you placed there by hand can need placing again.
A record of what the app has done since it started: playback, sync, network and errors. Nothing here is sent anywhere, and it is cleared when the app closes.
Readings used to check a build against its acceptance cases. Nothing here changes how the app behaves.
Tap a library to open on it. With none chosen, the shelf shows every library you can see.
No libraries yet. They appear after the first sync.
This server did not report a version.
This server has been checked. Each feature below is used only where support was confirmed; anything not confirmed is treated as unsupported.
This server has not been checked yet, so no feature list can be shown. Nothing is treated as supported until it has been checked.
What this app has saved. Two accounts share a server\'s books, so a number can be larger than what you can see.
Two accounts on one server count once.
Encrypted files. Signing a profile out removes its own.
Everything saved for this server, including libraries this profile cannot open.
Kept until nothing local still needs them.
Listening sessions this device recorded, and what the server did with them.
One per book started, kept for seven days after upload.
Should fall to 0 within a minute of playing while online.
Not a failure. The server already held a newer position for that book.
%1$s — more than five minutes. This device will win progress conflicts it should lose.
Each line says what to do and what this screen should then show. Marked automatically where the app can tell.
Play a minute, then watch “Waiting to upload” reach 0.
Confirm “Last accepted” moves while a book plays.
Turn off the network, play a minute, pause: “Waiting to upload” rises.
Turn the network back on: it falls again without replaying anything.
Kill the app mid-book, reopen it, and check the book resumes within 10 seconds of where it was.
Rewind five minutes deliberately, wait for a sync, and confirm the server keeps the earlier position.
Set the device clock five minutes ahead and confirm the warning below appears.
With a second device, listen further there and confirm this one does not overwrite it.
PLAY-001 needs a notification with transport controls while a book plays. These say whether one can appear.
Android 13 and later ask for this the first time a book plays. Declining it hides the notification and nothing else.
Play something, then come back. Yes here and nothing in the shade would be a real defect.
Play a book, pull down the shade: the media notification is there with working controls.
Auto lists media apps by what they declare, not by what they can play. The first two rows are this build; the rest are the phone.
The manifest entry Auto enumerates media apps by. No here means the app cannot appear in any car.
An exported service answering the media-browse action. This is what a head unit binds to.
The phone half of Android Auto. Without it there is nothing to list the app.

Android Auto hides apps it did not get from Play. In the Android Auto app: tap the version ten times to unlock Developer settings, then turn on Unknown sources — unlocking developer settings does not turn it on by itself. Force-stop Android Auto afterwards so it rebuilds its list.
Connect a head unit: BookWave is in the media app list and browses. If Last car connection still says never, no car ever reached the app.
Notifications are off, so this book has no notification or lock-screen controls.
This speed is remembered for this book. Other books use the default from Settings.
Used by every book that has not been given its own speed in the player.
The buttons show the number where an icon exists for it, and the amount is always announced.
Off by default. Never crosses a chapter start, never applies after you move the position yourself, and never after a call or a navigation prompt.
Streamed books only; a downloaded book uses the player\'s own defaults. A larger buffer survives a worse connection and uses more memory and mobile data. Takes effect the next time a book starts.

A book is marked finished when a little of it is left, so the last few seconds of credits do not leave it looking unread. How little is your server\'s decision, set per library — in the Audiobookshelf web interface, under that library\'s settings, as “mark as finished when time remaining is”. BookWave follows it rather than keeping a second opinion. Marking a book finished by hand always works either way, and starting a finished book from the beginning always un-finishes it.
